findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:263 — [P2, confidence 100] `@include flexbox();` makes the existing `.small-action button { float: right; }` at line 309 inert because floats do not apply to flex items, so action buttons render immediately after the description instead of at the row’s right edge; although flexbox replaces the float layout, the replacement supplies neither `margin-left: auto` nor a growing description, so the regression survives that counterargument.

app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:125 — [P3 advisory, confidence 75] `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val; ... order: $val;` assigns one number to incompatible ordinal models (legacy groups are one-based while modern order is zero-based), so a caller using the modern default `@include order(0)` gets valid modern CSS but an invalid ignored legacy declaration and inconsistent child order; although current call sites pass 2 and 3, the global mixin promises reusable ordering semantics, and splitting legacy/modern values or deleting the obsolete box-model declarations removes four compatibility branches.

app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic.scss:29 — [P3 advisory, confidence 50] global `.extra-info-wrapper { @include order(2); }` hides a header-child ordering rule outside the flex container that owns it, so reusing this generic wrapper under another flex parent silently moves it after default-order siblings; although `order` is inert outside flex layouts, that counterargument fails exactly when the next flex-based reuse activates it, and nesting this rule under `.d-header .contents` deletes the global coupling and one scattered ordering site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic.scss:29 — [P3 advisory, confidence 50] global `.extra-info-wrapper { @include order(2); }` hides a header-child ordering rule outside the flex container that owns it, so reusing this generic wrapper under another flex parent silently moves it after default-order siblings; although `order` is inert outside flex layouts, that counterargument fails exactly when the next flex-based reuse activates it, and nesting this rule under `.d-header .contents` deletes the global coupling and one scattered ordering site.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real architectural concern: `.extra-info-wrapper` is given `@include order(2)` at a global scope in topic.scss, but the flex container that makes this meaningful (`.d-header .contents` with `@include flexbox()`) is defined separately in header.scss. This creates implicit coupling - the order property only works when the element is a child of a flex container, and placing it globally means if `.extra-info-wrapper` is reused elsewhere under a different flex parent, it would unexpectedly have order:2. The suggestion to nest this rule under `.d-header .contents` to make the relationship explicit is a valid architectural improvement, though not a bug since the current code works correctly in its intended context.
